project.name: Aurum
project.previous_name: The Edge Lab (package 'edgelab'), renamed 2026-11-28 at the owner's request
project.what_it_is: An autonomous research laboratory that reverse-engineers why discretionary XAUUSD (gold) trades succeed or fail: it reconstructs trading decisions candle by candle, classifies mistakes, replays every trade under alternative decisions, tests hypotheses with strict out-of-sample discipline, and feeds what it learns back into the owner's live alert bot (signals.py).
project.what_it_is_not: Not a trading bot. It never connects to a broker, never places orders, never gives trading advice.

owner_brief.core_objective: Reverse-engineer the underlying principles of profitable discretionary trading by systematically investigating bad trades, failed setups, execution mistakes, misleading price action and successful trades.
phases_requested: 4 Success vs failure comparison of look-alike setups
6 Personal edge profiling (attempt to disprove the self-assessment)
later_requests: Test every possible combination of mistakes and their remedy
Make my bot understand the anatomy and essence of losing trades so it can better catch good trades
Rename it and provide a JSON that explains everything

built: Data layer on the repo's Dukascopy files: H1 2003-2026, M15 2008-2026, H4/D1 on the 17:00 New York close, FOMC/CPI/NFP windows, FRED macro lagged one day.
Causal features (116 columns), swing structure that only becomes known after confirmation, causal daily regimes.
16 discretionary setup archetypes x long/short, each tied to the conventional claim it embodies.
M15-resolved execution simulator: spread + slippage, worse costs in news and rollover, gap fills, stop-first ambiguity.
Mistake taxonomy (56 categories: ex-ante, ex-post, execution), each with a measurable rule and a statistical verdict.
17 counterfactual replays per trade, with hindsight kept separate from policy.
Look-alike winner/loser matching, condition scan, walk-forward ML meta-labelling, append-only experiment ledger and engine.
Truncation-based look-ahead audit, tests, and a single-file dashboard.
findings: No textbook setup had an out-of-sample edge, even before costs.
The condition scan produced fewer significant cells than chance.
'Late entry after the move' was contradicted: chasing did better (+0.17R / +0.19R).
Look-alike winners and losers differed by only a few hundredths of a standard deviation.
In hindsight 'take the opposite trade' rescued 49% of losers but adds nothing as a rule.

built: Trailing and partial exits; two momentum setups; H4/daily 'significant' levels; event studies.
Two-feature interaction scan; White's Reality Check, studentised test and Romano-Wolf step-down over the family.
Per-discovery stress tests (threshold neighbourhood, cost multiples, years, Monte-Carlo drawdown, same-month drift benchmark).
Forward-test registry; H1 extended from M15.
findings: The whole hypothesis family failed the Reality Check; nothing survived Romano-Wolf.
Momentum is real (0.1-0.3 ATR beyond drift) but too small to trade alone.
Pushing continuation trades into higher-timeframe levels did better, not worse.
Model-selected longs held on a 3 ATR trail after +1R looked validated, but the holdout was contaminated (see integrity log).

built: Direct Dukascopy updater (BID minute candles -> M15), verified to match the existing files exactly.
`cycle` command: update -> pre-registered agenda -> engine -> Reality Check -> freeze & forward-score -> research log -> dashboard.
Fixed holdout (2022-01 .. 2026-11-23) plus a 'forward' split for all later data.
Weekly Claude research session (scheduled task) and a GitHub Actions workflow (active once merged to main).
Holdout sealed in every descriptive view after a design leak was found.
findings: The pre-registered 'late entry + wide stop' idea passed all splits, but its design had seen pooled holdout verdicts.
Cycles kept producing a few validated variants; none passed family-wise correction.

timeline.stage: Round 3: every mistake x every remedy
built: Composite remedies: 5 entry x 4 stop x 8 exit fixes + skip + opposite = 162 per trade (~11 million re-simulations).
Atlas over 40 ex-ante mistakes, all pairs and supported triples, per side and per setup: 2,035,040 cells, all counted as trials.
Hindsight map for ex-post diagnoses.
findings: Remedies that reduce losses replicate (25,192 cells vs ~4,220 expected by luck; 71% sign agreement).
Profit does not replicate (43% sign agreement, worse than a coin flip).
Best ingredients: waiting for a confirming close (helps in 87% of cells) and a 3 ATR trail after +1R (79%). Waiting 3 bars hurts.

timeline.stage: Round 4: anatomy of the live bot's losing trades
built: Replay of signals.py's own strategies (trend, 4H trend, inside-day): 1,968 trades since 2008, same counts the bot publishes.
Ex-ante, in-trade and loss-type anatomy; pre-declared rules scored once on the holdout.
Stdlib 'anatomy' code inside signals.py: warning-sign line on setup alerts, flags saved in the journal, opt-in '3 hours in' note, opt-in skip rule. 99.9% parity with the lab.
findings: Before entry the bot's losers look like its winners; the one consistent warning sign is H1/4H/daily trend disagreement.
68% of losers never reach +0.5R (winners: 4%), but cutting slow starters early lowered expectancy in all 18 versions tested.
Trailing exits and the 4H conflict skip were positive or neutral on the holdout, not strong enough to change live trading yet.

built: Package renamed to 'aurum'; HISTORY.json generated from the live record and rebuilt every cycle.

methodology.decision_rule: Every decision is made at the close of an H1 bar using only information known then; higher-timeframe bars attach only after their scheduled close.

what_each_split_is_for.archive: 2003-07, H1 only: robustness in a very different regime.
what_each_split_is_for.holdout: Scored once per hypothesis, only after validation passes. Sealed in all descriptive views.
what_each_split_is_for.forward: Data after 2026-11-23: only frozen hypotheses are scored here, from their freeze time onward.

gates.holdout: n>=15, avg R>0, t>=1 (else weak or contradicted)

methodology.multiple_testing: Every scan cell, atlas cell and engine test is a trial (plus 1,430 legacy trials). BH-FDR, deflated Sharpe, White's Reality Check, studentised SPA-style test and Romano-Wolf step-down.
methodology.look_ahead_audit: Features and setup signals are rebuilt on data truncated at random bars and must be identical to full-history values.
methodology.units: R = profit or loss divided by the initial risk, after spread and slippage.

modules.__init__.py: AURUM — a research environment for reverse-engineering discretionary trading decisions on XAUUSD.
modules.atlas.py: The Mistake x Remedy atlas: every combination of ex-ante mistakes x every composite remedy.
modules.behaviour.py: Why does price behave the way it does around decisions? Market-level studies.
modules.bot_anatomy.py: Anatomy of the live bot's losing trades (signals.py), using the lab's tools.
modules.comparison.py: Success vs failure: compare trades that LOOKED the same but ended differently.
modules.config.py: Central configuration: paths, chronological splits, cost model, defaults.
modules.counterfactual.py: Counterfactual replay: what if the same decision had been executed differently?
modules.cycle.py: One autonomous research cycle. Designed to be run on a schedule, forever.
modules.dashboard.py: Build lab_output/dashboard.html: a single self-contained research dashboard.
modules.data.py: Historical data loading, cleaning, multi-timeframe construction.
modules.discovery.py: Edge discovery: exhaustive condition scan + walk-forward machine learning.
modules.forward.py: Forward test: the only data no hypothesis has ever seen.
modules.frame.py: Build the decision frame: H1 bars + causal features + structure + H4/D1 context.
modules.history.py: Builds aurum/HISTORY.json: the whole project explained, from its creation to now.
modules.hypothesis.py: Hypothesis specification + evaluation on the trade universe.
modules.regimes.py: Causal market-regime classification on daily bars.
modules.remedies.py: Composite remedies: every trade re-executed under ENTRY x STOP x EXIT fixes.
modules.robustness.py: Robustness and data-snooping controls for the whole hypothesis family.
modules.setups.py: Discretionary setup archetypes, reconstructed as decision points.
modules.structure.py: Market structure: confirmed swing points, trend structure, S/R levels, liquidity.
modules.trades.py: Turn decisions into simulated trades with a full context snapshot.
modules.updater.py: Incremental XAUUSD data updater (Dukascopy public datafeed, BID minute candles -> M15).

commands.python -m aurum cycle --budget N: one research cycle (used by the schedulers)
commands.python -m aurum run --budget N: full run without the update/log steps
